topic: How does defocused feed array placement optimize coverage versus scan loss in DBF architectures?
consensus_response: Defocused feed array placement optimizes coverage by reducing taper loss and enhancing robustness against feed failures. Adaptive beamforming stabilizes gain, while OFDM techniques optimize spectral efficiency. This combination ensures robust coverage and high data throughput, even with slight increases in spillover and unit cell losses.
reference_context: Defocused arrays reduce taper loss, increasing robustness against failures, with trade-offs in spillover and unit cell losses, as seen in Ku-band reflectarray antennas.
